sources: National List of Essential Medicines India 2022 (NLEM)

metadata.disclaimer: This database is for educational reference only. Always consult a licensed doctor or pharmacist before taking any medicine.

standard_dose.adult: 500mg to 1000mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed
standard_dose.child: 10 to 15 mg/kg every 4 to 6 hours (max 5 doses in 24 hours)

cautions: Avoid alcohol while taking
Use with caution in liver or kidney disease
Do not exceed recommended dose
medicines.pregnancy_note: Generally considered safe at recommended doses. Preferred pain reliever during pregnancy.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

standard_dose.adult: 200mg to 400mg every 6 to 8 hours with food
standard_dose.child: 5 to 10 mg/kg every 6 to 8 hours (for children over 6 months)

cautions: Always take with food or milk to protect stomach
Avoid in elderly with kidney problems
Short-term use only for OTC
Avoid if dehydrated
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in third trimester. Not recommended in first and second trimester without doctor advice.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.adult: 300mg to 600mg every 4 to 6 hours for pain/fever
standard_dose.cardiac_dose: 75mg to 150mg once daily (only under medical supervision)
standard_dose.max_daily_adult: 4000mg for pain (not recommended for prolonged use)

cautions: Never give to children with viral infections
Take with food
Do not use in dengue — increases bleeding risk
Avoid before surgery
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid especially in third trimester. Low-dose aspirin for pre-eclampsia prevention only under medical supervision.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 250mg to 500mg every 8 hours for 5 to 7 days

cautions: Complete the full course even if feeling better
Take with or without food
Watch for allergic reactions (rash, swelling, breathing difficulty)
Not effective against viral infections
medicines.pregnancy_note: Generally considered safe during pregnancy. Preferred antibiotic when needed.
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. Do not take without a doctor's prescription.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

standard_dose.adult: 500mg on day 1, then 250mg once daily for 4 days (Z-pack)
standard_dose.child: 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg for 4 days

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to azithromycin or macrolide antibiotics
History of QT prolongation (heart rhythm problem)
cautions: Take on empty stomach for better absorption
Inform doctor of heart conditions
Complete full course
May cause diarrhea
interactions: Antacids containing aluminium/magnesium (reduce absorption — take 2 hours apart)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Use only if clearly necessary and no safer alternative available. Consult doctor.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 250mg to 750mg every 12 hours for 3 to 14 days depending on infection

cautions: Avoid in children and adolescents
Risk of tendon rupture especially in elderly
Drink plenty of water
Avoid antacids within 2 hours
Avoid prolonged sun exposure
interactions: Antacids, iron, zinc supplements (severely reduce absorption)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Avoid.
medicines.prescription_note: SCHEDULE H1 — Requires restricted prescription. Serious antibiotic — must not be taken without prescription.
medicines.source: NLEM 2022, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022, Drugs and Cosmetics Act Schedule H1

standard_dose.adult: 500mg twice daily with meals, increasing gradually to 1000mg to 2000mg daily

cautions: Always take with food to reduce stomach upset
Stop before contrast dye procedures (CT scan, angiogram)
Monitor kidney function regularly
Do not skip meals
interactions: Contrast dyes (kidney damage — stop 48 hours before)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Generally avoided in pregnancy. Insulin is preferred. Discuss with doctor.
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. For diabetes management only.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

used_for: Prevention of heart attack and stroke

standard_dose.adult: 10mg to 80mg once daily, usually at bedtime

cautions: Report muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine immediately (rhabdomyolysis)
Regular liver function tests
Avoid grapefruit juice
Do not stop without doctor advice
medicines.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Stop immediately if pregnant.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 20mg once daily before breakfast for 4 to 8 weeks

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole or other PPIs
cautions: Do not use for more than 14 days without doctor advice
Take 30 to 60 minutes before meals
Long-term use may reduce magnesium and B12 levels
May mask symptoms of stomach cancer
interactions: Clopidogrel (reduces anti-platelet effect — important for heart patients)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Use only if clearly necessary. Antacids generally preferred in pregnancy.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

used_for: Prevention of ulcers in patients on NSAIDs

standard_dose.adult: 40mg once daily before breakfast

cautions: Take before meals
Short-term use recommended
Long-term use — risk of fractures, low magnesium, low B12
medicines.pregnancy_note: Use only if clearly necessary.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.adult: 10mg once daily

contraindications: Known allergy to cetirizine or hydroxyzine
cautions: May cause drowsiness in some people — caution while driving
Avoid alcohol
Take at night if drowsiness is a concern
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid if possible. Consult doctor before use.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 10mg once daily

cautions: Less sedating than first-generation antihistamines
Use with caution in liver disease
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid if possible. Discuss with doctor.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023

standard_dose.adult: 400mg to 800mg three times daily for 5 to 10 days depending on condition

contraindications: Known allergy to metronidazole or nitroimidazoles
cautions: STRICTLY AVOID ALCOHOL during treatment and 48 hours after (severe disulfiram-like reaction)
May cause nausea, metallic taste
Complete the full course
interactions: Alcohol (DANGEROUS — causes severe nausea, vomiting, flushing)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in first trimester. Use with caution in second and third trimester only when clearly necessary.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

used_for: Angina (chest pain due to heart disease)

standard_dose.adult: 5mg once daily, may be increased to 10mg once daily

cautions: Do not stop suddenly without doctor advice
Monitor blood pressure regularly
May cause ankle swelling
Avoid grapefruit juice
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in pregnancy. Use antihypertensives approved for pregnancy (methyldopa, labetalol).
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. Do not stop without doctor guidance.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

standard_dose.adult: 50mg once daily, may be increased to 100mg once daily

cautions: Monitor potassium levels — can cause high potassium (hyperkalemia)
Do not use with potassium supplements without doctor advice
Monitor kidney function
interactions: Potassium supplements / potassium-sparing diuretics (dangerous high potassium)
NSAIDs (reduced blood pressure control, kidney risk)
medicines.pregnancy_note: CONTRAINDICATED in all trimesters of pregnancy. Can cause serious fetal harm.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 25mg to 100mg once daily

contraindications: Second and third degree heart block
cautions: NEVER stop suddenly — must taper gradually under doctor supervision (risk of heart attack)
Can mask hypoglycemia symptoms in diabetics
Avoid in asthma — can trigger severe bronchospasm
interactions: Clonidine (stopping clonidine suddenly while on atenolol — severe hypertension)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Use with caution. Can cause fetal growth restriction. Only under specialist care.
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. Never stop without tapering.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

standard_dose.adult: 1 litre (1 packet dissolved in 1 litre clean water) — drink small amounts frequently
standard_dose.child_under_2: 50 to 100 ml after every loose stool
standard_dose.child_2_to_10: 100 to 200 ml after every loose stool
standard_dose.preparation: Dissolve 1 ORS sachet in exactly 1 litre of clean/boiled water. Do not add extra water or sugar.

cautions: Prepare with correct amount of water only
Do not boil the solution after preparation
Discard unused solution after 24 hours
Seek hospital if child is unable to drink, has bloody stools, or high fever
medicines.pregnancy_note: Safe and recommended during pregnancy for dehydration.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022, UNICEF Guidelines

used_for: Diarrhoea in children (reduces severity and duration)
cautions: Use alongside ORS in childhood diarrhoea (WHO/UNICEF recommendation)
May cause vomiting if given on empty stomach
interactions: Iron supplements (reduce zinc absorption — take separately)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Safe at recommended doses.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022, WHO Diarrhoea Treatment Guidelines

standard_dose.adult: 1 to 2 tablets or 10ml suspension 20 to 60 minutes after meals and at bedtime
standard_dose.max_daily_adult: Follow label instructions. Not for continuous daily use beyond 2 weeks.

cautions: Separate from other medicines by at least 2 hours — antacids interfere with absorption of many drugs
Do not use for more than 2 weeks without doctor advice
interactions: Most oral medicines — take 2 hours apart
medicines.pregnancy_note: Generally safe for short-term use in pregnancy.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.adult: 10mg up to three times daily before meals

cautions: Do not exceed recommended dose
Short courses recommended
Consult doctor for heart conditions
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in pregnancy. Consult doctor.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

used_for: Nausea and vomiting due to chemotherapy

standard_dose.adult: 4mg to 8mg every 8 hours

cautions: Monitor heart rhythm in high doses
Use with caution in liver disease
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in first trimester. Use in later pregnancy only under medical supervision.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 4mg every 4 to 6 hours

cautions: CAUSES SIGNIFICANT DROWSINESS — do not drive or operate machinery
Avoid alcohol
Use with caution in elderly
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid if possible, especially near delivery.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.adult: 10mg to 30mg every 4 to 8 hours

cautions: Not for productive cough (cough with phlegm)
Not for children under 6
Risk of misuse in high doses
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid especially in first trimester.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 30mg three times daily for first 2 to 3 days, then 30mg twice daily

cautions: Drink plenty of fluids while taking
Not for dry cough
interactions: Antibiotics (ambroxol may increase antibiotic levels in lung tissue — beneficial effect)
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid in first trimester. Use with caution in second and third trimester.
medicines.source: CIMS India 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.adult: One tablet (usually 60mg elemental iron + 500mcg folic acid) once or twice daily
standard_dose.pregnant_women: One tablet daily as per government NLEM programme

cautions: Take on empty stomach for best absorption or with Vitamin C
May cause constipation, dark stools, nausea
Keep away from children (iron overdose is dangerous)
Separate from antacids, tea, coffee, milk by at least 2 hours
medicines.pregnancy_note: Recommended and essential during pregnancy. Part of national anaemia prevention programme.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022, National Iron Plus Initiative India

standard_dose.adult_deficiency: 60,000 IU weekly for 8 weeks, then maintenance 1000 to 2000 IU daily
standard_dose.child: As prescribed based on blood levels

cautions: Do not exceed recommended dose — fat soluble and can accumulate
Check blood calcium and Vitamin D levels
Sun exposure is the best natural source
medicines.pregnancy_note: Safe and recommended during pregnancy at appropriate doses.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, ICMR Guidelines India

standard_dose.adult: 1mg to 4mg once daily with breakfast

cautions: Risk of hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar) — especially if meal is skipped
Carry glucose tablets or sugar
Avoid alcohol
Regular blood sugar monitoring
medicines.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Use insulin instead.
medicines.source: NLEM 2022, WHO Essential Medicines List 2023

used_for: Type 2 Diabetes not controlled by oral medicines

standard_dose.note: Dose is highly individualised — set by doctor based on blood sugar levels. Never adjust without medical advice.

contraindications: Hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar — requires dose reduction not more insulin)
cautions: Store in refrigerator (2 to 8°C)
NEVER freeze
Rotate injection sites
Check blood sugar regularly
Carry fast sugar (glucose, candy) at all times
Learn hypoglycaemia symptoms and management
medicines.pregnancy_note: Insulin is the preferred antidiabetic in pregnancy. Safe and recommended.
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. Never self-adjust dose.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022

standard_dose.adult: Varies widely by condition — 5mg to 60mg daily. Set by doctor only.
standard_dose.note: Dose and duration must be determined by a doctor.

cautions: NEVER stop suddenly after long-term use — must taper gradually
Increases blood sugar (monitor in diabetics)
Increases infection risk
Can cause weight gain, mood changes, osteoporosis with long-term use
Take with food
medicines.pregnancy_note: Use only if clearly necessary and under specialist care.
medicines.prescription_note: PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED — Schedule H. Never self-prescribe steroids. Never stop abruptly.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, Indian Pharmacopoeia 2022

standard_dose.inhaler: 1 to 2 puffs (100mcg per puff) every 4 to 6 hours as needed
standard_dose.tablet_adult: 2mg to 4mg three to four times daily

cautions: Overuse indicates poor asthma control — seek doctor review
May cause tremors and fast heart rate
Have reliever inhaler available at all times
medicines.pregnancy_note: Inhaled salbutamol is generally safe during pregnancy for asthma attacks.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, NLEM 2022, GINA Guidelines 2023

standard_dose.adult: 100mg twice daily on day 1, then 100mg once daily

cautions: Take with full glass of water — do not lie down for 30 minutes after (esophageal ulcers)
Avoid direct sunlight (photosensitivity)
Do not take with dairy, antacids, iron within 2 hours
medicines.pregnancy_note: CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy — causes tooth discolouration and bone effects in fetus.
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

medicines.schedule: Schedule X — Requires special prescription, controlled substance

standard_dose.adult: 0.25mg to 2mg per day, as prescribed
standard_dose.note: Dose set by neurologist or psychiatrist only

cautions: HIGH DEPENDENCE POTENTIAL — do not take without prescription
Never stop suddenly (risk of withdrawal seizures)
Causes sedation — do not drive
Avoid alcohol absolutely
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid. Can cause neonatal withdrawal syndrome and respiratory depression in newborn.
medicines.prescription_note: SCHEDULE X — CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE. Requires special prescription. High addiction potential. Never self-prescribe.
medicines.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act Schedule X, WHO Essential Medicines List 2023

standard_dose.adult: 50mg two to three times daily with food
standard_dose.topical_gel: Apply 2 to 4g to affected area 3 to 4 times daily

cautions: Always take with food
Short-term use preferred
Monitor blood pressure and kidney function with long-term use
Increased cardiovascular risk with long-term use
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid — especially in third trimester (can cause premature closure of ductus arteriosus).
medicines.source: WHO Essential Medicines List 2023, CIMS India 2023

standard_dose.adult: 50mg to 100mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed

cautions: DEPENDENCE POTENTIAL — use as short as possible
Causes drowsiness — do not drive
Lowers seizure threshold
Avoid alcohol absolutely
medicines.pregnancy_note: Avoid. Can cause neonatal withdrawal syndrome.
medicines.prescription_note: SCHEDULE H1 — RESTRICTED. Serious abuse and dependence potential. Never without prescription.
medicines.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act Schedule H1, WHO Essential Medicines List 2023
